MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The wireless earbuds felt useful because I have used wired headphones, and portable wireless listening would add a different use rather than simply replace what I own.",
    "The HDMI cable connects with my history of connecting devices, although I would need a specific reason to buy another cable, such as needing the extra length."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The Alexa speakers, smart display and smart plug assume I want a connected home, but my recent activity is about practical computer, networking and desk accessories.",
    "The streaming players do not address an immediate need. My Raspberry Pi purchases suggest an interest in building a setup, which does not automatically mean I want a separate streaming device.",
    "The tablet does not offer a clear next step for me: I already have a Kindle for reading, and my more recent choices focus on supporting existing equipment."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "Owning a Kindle seems to have been taken as interest in a much wider range of Amazon devices, even though those devices serve different purposes.",
    "My electronics purchases seem to have been treated as a broad interest in gadgets, overlooking whether each gadget helps with something I am currently doing."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My recent Ethernet adapter, Ethernet cables, headphone mount and computer duster point toward improving connectivity, organization and upkeep around my computer.",
    "What I already own matters: another HDMI cable needs a concrete purpose, while wireless earbuds could complement my wired headphones by supporting portable listening.",
    "My Raspberry Pi, case and power supply purchases belong together as a hands-on project; that connection matters more than a general association with home entertainment."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognized my interest in electronics but missed my current focus on useful additions to equipment I already own."
}
